key_insight: CPA-NAMD-extF extends classical-path nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to field-driven electronic responses, revealing fluctuation-sensitive opto-currents and Br-centered vortex currents in a 2D hybrid perovskite.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables efficient finite-temperature modeling of optical and electronic responses in large, structurally complex materials.
method: Propagate a first-principles electronic density matrix along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
Include explicit external-field coupling and self-consistent electronic-density updates.
Apply the framework to crystalline and amorphous SiO₂ and (BA)₂CsPb₂Br₇.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks show close agreement with regular TDDFT for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses; perovskite calculations reveal strong structural-fluctuation effects on second-order opto-current.
watch_item: Precomputed ionic trajectories retain the classical-path approximation, so field-induced feedback on ionic motion requires careful assessment.
paper_title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
